name: Apollo 17

terrain.note: Generic moon surface — no site-specific DTM available yet

objects.name: Challenger Descent Stage
objects.description: Lower half of Lunar Module Challenger. The last crewed spacecraft to land on the Moon. Cernan and Schmitt spent a record 75 hours on the surface with three EVAs totalling 22 hours.

objects.name: American Flag
objects.description: The last flag planted on the Moon. Cernan's final words on the surface: 'We leave as we came and, God willing, as we shall return, with peace and hope for all mankind.'

objects.name: Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-3)
objects.description: The third and final lunar rover. Cernan set the unofficial lunar speed record of 17.1 km/h on this vehicle. Parked at its final TV position to film the last human departure from the Moon.

objects.name: ALSEP Central Station
objects.description: Apollo 17's experiment suite — the most advanced of all Apollo packages. Included a lunar seismic profiling experiment, gravimeter, atmospheric composition experiment, and surface electrical properties experiment.

objects.name: Laser Ranging Retroreflector
objects.description: The last retroreflector placed on the Moon. Together with the Apollo 11, 14, and 15 reflectors plus two French-built reflectors on Soviet Lunokhod rovers, it forms a network still used for precision measurements.

objects.name: Orange Soil Discovery Site
objects.description: At Shorty Crater, Schmitt — the only geologist to walk on the Moon — discovered orange soil: tiny beads of volcanic glass erupted 3.7 billion years ago. One of the most important geological finds of the programme.

_note: Equipment positions approximate, based on Apollo 17 traverse maps and LROC imagery. Orange soil site at Shorty Crater, ~1.6km from LM (scaled down for gameplay).
